Preserve user preference for methods on meaningful owning types, RAII, sealed marker-trait typestate, immutable inputs and consuming transitions. Targeted follow-up only, no full review rerun. Round three's proposed unshare
control still cannot exercise clone. I reject that mechanism; the current marker
says namespace denial, not specifically clone-mask coverage, so retain historical
markers and document the actual gap.

Inspect the new uncommitted validation/rewrite-command-integration/clone-probe.c,
run.py and src/main.rs clone-filter mode and README. It is a separate benign C
fixture using libc clone directly with fixed flags and no shared VM, child only
returns zero, parent waits. Both arms require effective SYS_ADMIN and set NNP;
ordinary clone succeeds in both, seven namespace flags require baseline success
then EPERM under unchanged production CommandSyscalls::apply. Application Rust
remains forbid unsafe. No untrusted command runs with extra capabilities.

Actual disposable VM v262 is running. Its serial.txt already records all sixteen
control/filtered cases passing and NATIVE_CLONE_NAMESPACE_MASK_PASS. Do NOT claim
full-suite pass until verdict exists; inspect /var/tmp/conglobate-rewrite-v262.
The legacy CLONE_NEWTIME bit is in the exit signal byte, so not claimed as a time
namespace control. No host execution of probe or privileged actions. No edits.

Check whether this really closes tests-001 for supported legacy namespace flags,
find any concrete flaw in the probe or overclaim, and reconcile. The source archive
captured before run also has an accidental extra marker requirement on subset-mode
verdicts; current runner fixes that, while the full-mode behavior under test is
unchanged. Review that delta explicitly rather than claiming exact byte identity.
